analysis: The only change in SSDPrefixCache.swift is in retireIndexedEntries (head ~1793-1800). Previously one removalLock critical section guarded hasSafeRoot/ownsEvictionRoot and ran SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove over the whole URL list. Now SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices(urls) calls a closure per slice, and each slice takes removalLock and re-checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot before removing. Security-relevant effects: (1) The safe-root and ownership checks are made on every slice, so a successor taking the root between slices stops further unlinks. This is the fail-closed behavior the existing comment describes and is not weaker than before. (2) Unlinks go through the same SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove with root, index and epochStore, so the no-follow and safe-URL logic is unchanged. (3) The lock is released between slices, so index and file removal is no longer atomic across the whole batch. It still serializes against other removals per slice, and the comments already tolerate non-atomic races with a successor wipe. (4) If removeInSlices is implemented so that a nil slice result aborts the loop and returns an empty Result, behavior matches the old nil to .init() path. I did not see its implementation, so I cannot confirm how it aggregates removed, externalChange and partial results, or that it handles an empty list and a slice size of 0. Callers sweepExpiredEntries and budget eviction use result.removed and externalChange for stats and reconciliation. Cleanup, TTL and LRU purge behavior for T-041 (at-rest window bounds) is functionally intended to be unchanged; any bug in slicing that skipped entries would only delay expiry. Base text is a different region (startup scan, settleDurableDonation) and is unchanged. No regression is evidenced, but removeInSlices and its aggregation semantics sit in another file (the SSDOwnedEntryRetirement source) and were not supplied, so I recommend a check of it.
